title: To Elena
text:
A lily swings in the valley

so pure and so graceful

as April's candid morning.

The hummingbird that tenderly loves her,

jealous of her modesty and beauty,

does not dare to sip in her corolla

the delicious nectar;

he is deprived of nourishment

so that she may live lush and candid,

and he would die content

enjoying the perfumes of her breath:

enchanting Elena,

I am the hummingbird, you the lily.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the courtly flower-and-hummingbird conceit explicit.

title: To the Worthy and Wise Intendant Don Alejandro Ramírez
text:
Sad, beautiful Borinquen moaned

dragging miserable poverty,

she who contained the gift of perennial wealth

in her fertile fields.

Heaven, which lovingly loved her,

could not consent in its tenderness

that she should suffer such barbarous harshness,

she who did not deserve the yoke of evil;

It heard Power's high prayer

(grateful sigh of patriotic love)

and ordered that, to change the precarious era

into rich well-being, Ramiro should go...

Benefactor Ramiro, your noble history

Puerto Rico will engrave in its memory.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the civic sonnet's personified Borinquen and its praise of Ramírez.

title: The Eyes of ...
text:
Do you ask me, painter, how I wish

you to paint the gaze and beauty

of those eyes where Eden shines,

of those eyes for which I live and die?

Copy the radiance of the morning star,

the sweetness of a gentle gazelle,

the tenderness of the loving turtle-dove,

the shine of the flattering diamond.

You must paint them large and alive

where the blessed torch may shine

of noble meditation, very expressive,

With sweet undefined vagueness;

do you want to give them still more charms

of passionate love? give them life.
editorial_note: The translation follows the painterly instruction while keeping the formal address.

title: To Some Eyes
text:
Do you ask me, painter, how I wish

you to paint the gaze and beauty

of those eyes where Eden shines,

of those eyes for which I live and die?


Copy the radiance of the morning star,

the sweetness of a gentle gazelle,

the tenderness of the loving turtle-dove,

the shine of the flattering diamond.


You must paint them large and alive

where the blessed torch may shine

of noble meditation, very expressive.


With sweet undefined vagueness;

do you want to give them still more charms

of passionate love? Give them life.
editorial_note: This related version keeps the stanza breaks and final imperative capitalization of the source.

title: An Angel Descended to Pindus One Day...
text:
An angel descended to Pindus one day,

for him a muse of love sighed;

you were born, oh beautiful one, of that harmony.

Her inspired brow, her ambrosial voice,

the Muse gave you.


She gave you, as mother, her enchanting form,

her nymph's step, her plaint of love,

her moon eyes and gentle hair;

while the angel, from celestial sphere,

gave you radiance.


A song of joy sounded on Olympus,

then heaven sorrowfully moaned;

the former joyfully acquired a virgin,

heaven lost a beloved angel

and the world applauded.


And you before the applause, incautious, ah! forget

that God formed the angel for heaven.

I weep illusions, how sadly lost,

seeing your wings already sold to the world...

An angel, you?... No longer.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the mythological register and the poem's final disillusionment.

title: God Greets You, Oh Mary...
text:
CHOIR

God greets you, oh Mary:

you brought love to the earth

and man in his helplessness

called you "Providence."


Full you are of eternal grace,

precious flower

and loving

that the Eternal One cultivated;

and when to earth you were

sent,

perfumed,

forever it remained.


The Lord is with you:

his clemency

and high essence

he gave you, immortal virgin;

blessed among women,

the most beautiful,

like a star

heavenly light and guide.


And blessed has been the fruit

fortunate

that lovingly

Gabriel announced to the world,

for with his cherished blood

and his cross and

his light

he redeemed us from Lucifer.


If the angels sing to you

melodies,

what joys

they give to your egregious mansion;

angels are we

loved by you,

exiled ones!...

Give us then your blessing.
editorial_note: The hymn structure and short stepped devotional lines are preserved in English.

title: The Sun of Fortune...
text:
I

The sun of fortune

has not yet given my eyes

your image; my cravings

perceive your beauty,

perceive on high

the gleam of an angel,

the beautiful face of a fairy...

To call my sad fate happy,

angel, fairy, or woman, I long to see you.


II

Love inspires me, the bird

messenger of the air,

that carries to the high sphere

like a heavenly ship

love's gentle song;

love also inspires me,

the flower that breathes aroma,

and such joy your name pours into my being,

that flower, bird, or woman, I die to see you.


III

I do not know if you are a morning star

that announces a joyful day,

or in shadowy storm

offers a course

to the sad sailor;

yet angel or fairy,

or precious bird or flower,

or magic star;

to love life more than death,

my longing, lady, is to know you.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the three-part courtly ascent through angel, fairy, bird, flower, and star.

title: The Prayer of a Virgin
text:
Elena


Solitary and fearful,

poor helpless vessel,

I wander on the sea of life

in unequal combat.

Why, oh heaven, did you rob me

of sweet maternal shelter?

What shall I be without her dear love

before the fierce gale?


Sad orphan of the world

on the deserted deep,

who in calm weather toward the harbor

will generously guide me?

What pilot among the rocks

that the treacherous sea hides,

from its harmful fury,

ah me, will save me?


If you, benevolent heaven,

deny me daylight,

and hide in shadowy night

the star of salvation;

from disastrous shipwreck

can I free myself, alas sad one,

when the reef that exists

is my own heart?


Oh destiny, be merciful

to the poor abandoned one

who without support, trusting,

gives herself at your mercy.

From the savage storm,

from the mysterious reef,

deliver me, loving heaven,

deliver me, heaven, from myself.
editorial_note: The translation follows the extended shipwreck metaphor and treats sana as the likely saña in context.

title: The Sound Approaches...
text:
The sound

approaches. The soul becomes young again

Submitting to the overwhelming whisper.

In dreams, breathless, I press against my lips

Your passing hand.


I dream I am a boy again, a lover again,

I see a ravine and wild grasses.

And in those grasses a thorny thicket

In the mist of evening.


Through the flowers, leaves and thorny branches

The old house looks into my heart

The sky peers again, blushing from side to side,

Your window.

This voice

is yours and I would give life and pain

For its incomprehensible sound,

Though in the dream I press against my lips

Your beloved passing hand.

May 2

1912

Version by Jorge Bustamante García
editorial_note: The translation preserves the dated version note and the recurrent passing hand.
